thread.title: Note to Musk: Tesla isn't the only company targeted by short sellers. Here's who tops the list.

author: Jeff Jeffrey
title: Note to Musk: Tesla isn't the only company targeted by short sellers. Here's who tops the list.
text: – National Digital Producer, The Business Journals, Aug 9, 2018, 6:34am PDT Elon Musk took some obvious — and not so obvious — swipes at investors betting against Tesla Inc. this week by disclosing his hope to take the carmaker private at a significant premium to its current stock price. His neighbors in Silicon Valley might want to pay attention. As of Aug. 7, Tesla (Nasdaq: TSLA) ranked as the country's top target for so-called short sellers, or investors whose bets stand to make money if a company's share price declines. The short positions affected approximately 34 million Tesla shares valued at about $13.2 billion, or about 20 percent of the company's entire stock market value as of Tuesday's close. Tesla is not the only Silicon Valley company to draw significant bets against its stock price; of the 20 companies to attract the most short interest as of Aug. 7, 13 hailed from the tech sector. Among those technology giants, nine were based in Silicon Valley. Ranked second behind Tesla was Apple Inc ., the trillion-dollar computer and smartphone maker which had some $8.9 billion in wagers against its stock as of Aug. 7. Rounding out the top five were Amazon .com ($7.8 billion), Netflix Inc. ($5.8 billion) and Microsoft Corp. ($5.1 billion). Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL), Amazon (Nasdaq: AMZN) and Netflix (Nasdaq: NFLX) are all based in Silicon Valley, while Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT) has some of its largest operations stretching along the valley from Palo Alto to San Jose. Facebook (Nasdaq: FB), which saw the largest single-day stock slide ever on July 26, just missed the top five with its short interest topping $4.5 billion as of Tuesday's close. A Business Journals analysis of roughly 3,400 public companies found that stocks targeted by short sellers slipped to 17.9 billion shares as of Aug. 7 versus 18.7 billion shares a month earlier. Following Musk's Aug. 7 announcement that he was “considering taking Tesla private at $420” per share, Tesla's shares rose from around $350 per share to $379.57 as of that day's close. Analysts estimate the day's stock movement erased around $1.3 billion in value held by short investors. Tesla's shares dropped to $370.34 as of the following day's close. – National Digital Producer, The Business Journals, Aug 9, 2018, 6:34am PDT Tuesday, August 14, 2018 Join us to celebrate summer at our BizMix and Brews at Scott's Seafood.
